v.why: Parallel 3x3 convs summed at node 3 are partly substitutable, so the gain from a conv on edge 5 shrinks when edge 4 already supplies one.
An input-to-output identity is most valuable when it residualizes a deep conv chain starting with a conv on edge 0.
A strong conv on edge 5 dominates node 3's sum, diluting a pooled edge-4 route and softening the harm of replacing a learnable op there.
Conv capacity already entering node 3 from node 1 makes a direct input-to-output conv partly redundant.
When node 2 already receives conv features directly from the input via edge 1, a second conv input via edge 2 offers diminishing returns.
An identity shortcut from input to output residualizes the deep conv path through node 2, so a conv on edge 5 trains better and helps more.
Without a direct input-to-output edge, node 1 to node 3 becomes the main shallow route, so adding conv capacity there matters more.
A skip from node 1 forwards edge-0 conv features straight to the output, so it acts as a learned route rather than a raw input copy.
Without edge 3, node 3 depends on node 1 via edges 4 and 2-5, so emptying node 1 removes most paths to the output.
If edge 0 is none, edge 1 is node 2's only source of input, so cutting it empties node 2 and the edge-5 route entirely.
